budgetRationale: a proof follow-up step in the consumer release, its admission in the release-tag push route without a second approval, regression cases in the release, guard-push and close-path walk suites; no grant planned
title: The push and release approval proofs of an audited commit reach the remote audit bundle in one evidence-only follow-up commit
goal: Candidate 20e (PO tile decision 2026-11-08: the push/release approval proof is added afterwards as its own evidence file under audit-bundles/<feature>/<commit>/proofs/ in the release commit and pushed with the version tag; the bundle itself stays unchanged, create-only, only the file is added). Background: since candidate 20d (w275) the one-shot close writes audit-bundles/<feature>/<commit>/ with proofs/ (design approval, reconcile) and commits it in the close commit; the push approval signs exactly that commit, so its proof can never sit inside it, and the release approval comes even later. Build, runner-neutral: (1) the consumer release route (scripts/release-preflight-cli.mjs consumer mode, lib/consumer-release.mjs) gains, after a ready release approval, one step that writes the public proof objects of the push approval and the release approval for exactly the approved commit (lib/audit-proof-collection.mjs already reads the push envelope by forCommit; never a private key, only the public proof object; a chat-mode approval is carried as an attribution record, never as a proof) as new files into audit-bundles/<feature>/<approved commit>/proofs/ plus one appended manifest entry file that lists them (the existing manifest and README bytes stay unchanged, so the bundle's own verify still passes; `audit-bundle.mjs verify` learns to also check the follow-up file when present), arms the writer commit capability (G20-66, armWriterCommitCapability) for exactly those files, and prints the commit step; (2) the release-tag push admission (hooks/guard-push.mjs authorizeRecordedReleaseTag, G20-42b) admits pushing the branch to exactly ONE commit on top of the approved commit whose diff ONLY adds files under audit-bundles/<feature>/<approved commit>/proofs/ (and that follow-up manifest file), together with the annotated release tag that still peels to the approved commit; anything else in that commit falls through to the full gate unchanged; (3) docs/push-release-flow.md (consumer release section) names the step. If admitting the follow-up commit needs any weaker check than today's push gate for every other content, STOP (see stops). Restate in place with a comment any test that pins the old release output (QG-04). Regression cases: the follow-up commit with only proof files is pushed with the tag without a second approval; a follow-up commit that touches any other path is refused by the full gate; the bundle verifies before and after the follow-up; a chat-mode project carries an attribution record, not a proof. Developed and tested in the clone named in facts; delivered as the held patch specs/sprint-alfred-epic/evidence/held-patches/w282-c20e-audit-push-proof-followup.patch.
facts: CLONE-SLICE ROUTE: the clone is scratch/agent-out/c20e-ap (a shared clone of BASE_SHA, the applied and stamped candidate 20d with the 20e sibling patches); first step: `git -C scratch/agent-out/c20e-ap rev-parse HEAD` must print that SHA, otherwise STOP. Never run a git command that writes; use the helpers: `node scratch/agent-out/test-in.mjs scratch/agent-out/c20e-ap <test file> --private-tmp` (one suite at a time), `node scratch/agent-out/commit-in.mjs scratch/agent-out/c20e-ap "<conventional message>"`, `node scratch/agent-out/save-patch.mjs scratch/agent-out/c20e-ap BASE_SHA HEAD specs/sprint-alfred-epic/evidence/held-patches/w282-c20e-audit-push-proof-followup.patch`. The helper's `apply --check on repo` line is expected to fail: ignore it. A commit message must not contain the name of the version-control tool.

Write the three deliverables early; commit-in and save-patch after every green step. The final return JSON must carry every schema field including changedPaths (a missing field fails the host commit with NGHR-FINAL-SHAPE).

The check test is a plain node:test file (60 s, no product run): the .patch exists and is non-empty, every touched file is under plugins/pipeline-core/, harness/ or docs/ (docs only when the notes name them).

hooks/guard-push.test.mjs is a protected test (PGD*, PG-N27-TAG-06/07 pin the full gate for tags): add new cases in hooks/guard-push-release-tag-ancestry.test.mjs instead, as w270 did; never change an existing guard-push case.

PO rules: never fully blocking; runner and platform neutral; QG-04 restate in place with a comment; never re-pin the Critic preimage; a new kernel import must keep GMWKC01 (guard-maintenance-window-kernel-closure.test.mjs) green with the threat-model doc entry; a new auth verb or kind must keep harness/scripts/check-auth-gate-inventory-drift.test.mjs green.
Notes follow one existing held-patches *.notes.md (what / why / not changed / not proven); no absolute host paths; AC-108 closest criterion; PRD and Spec unchanged.
targeted: the suites next to every file you change, one at a time (release-preflight-cli, consumer-release, guard-push-release-tag-ancestry, audit-bundle lib and script, close-path-e2e, check-auth-gate-inventory-drift, GMWKC01)
forbidden: Do not run refresh-derived-files, the inventory rebaseline or full-verify.
Do not edit anything in the real checkout except the three w282 deliverables.
stops: Admitting the evidence-only follow-up commit would need a weaker check than today's push gate for any content other than the added proof files: write the notes with the smallest design that would not, change no code, and return.
A file that must change is covered by the Critic preimage pin or is a protected test (report the file; never re-pin, never edit the protected test).
